title: Shared Services Policy Cookbook and Process Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is a consolidated "cookbook" of company-wide policies, decision gates, and ready-to-use templates for Shared Services processes. It is intended for cross-functional teams (Engineering, Product, Finance, Security, People Ops, and Procurement) to standardize how we: manage access and permissions, run change control, classify and handle data, procure goods and services, onboard vendors, and approve travel and expenses.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and third-party vendors.
- Covers corporate and technical controls for systems and procurement valued under and over approval thresholds.
- Does not replace legal agreements for contract negotiation; use this as an operational overlay.

When to use this cookbook

1. New tool or vendor evaluation (procurement + security review).
2. Role changes requiring access updates.
3. Infrastructure or production changes that could impact SLOs.
4. Travel and expense requests requiring tiered approvals.

Quick reference: Approval matrix (high level)

| Item | Approver | Threshold | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SaaS subscription (non-sensitive) | Team Lead + Finance | < $10K/year | Use credit card if < $1K and on corporate card list |
| SaaS subscription (sensitive data) | Engineering Manager + Security + Finance | Any value | Requires security questionnaire and legal review |
| Cloud infra (new provider) | Infra Lead + Security + Finance | Any value | PoC requires security checklist and capacity plan |
| Capital equipment (GPU/Servers) | Procurement + Finance Director | > $25K | Requires asset tagging and depreciation code |

Access and permissions (standardized patterns)

Principles
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum set of privileges required and review quarterly.
- Temporary elevation: all elevated privileges must be timeboxed and documented.
- Separation of duties: procurement, approval, and payments should not be owned by the same individual for high-value purchases.

Access request flow (template)

1. Employee completes the Access Request Form (template below).
2. Requesting Manager verifies job justification and duration.
3. System owner approves or requests changes.
4. Security performs automatic policy checks (data access, MFA, device posture).
5. Provisioning executed via SSO or ticketed automation.

Access Request Form (sample fields)
- Requestor name: 
- Employee ID / Contractor company: 
- System or service name: 
- Reason / business justification: 
- Minimum role (read/write/admin): 
- Duration / expiry date: 
- Manager approver: 
- Security reviewer (if accessing PII or regulated data): 

Quarterly access review checklist
- Owner lists all active accounts and roles.
- Verify last activity timestamp; flag stale accounts (>90 days).
- Revoke or refresh temporary elevations.
- Document review in the Access Review Log (template: CSV).

Change management (engineered and operational changes)

Purpose: Ensure predictable, low-risk changes to production and shared systems.

Change categories
- Standard changes: routine, pre-approved (e.g., certificate renewals).
- Normal changes: scheduled, reviewed by Change Board.
- Emergency changes: applied immediately to mitigate critical incidents; post-facto review required.

Change submission template (required fields)
- Change ID: auto-generated (CHG-YYYYMMDD-####)
- Owner / Requestor: 
- Change type: (Standard / Normal / Emergency)
- Risk level: (Low / Medium / High) with justification
- Rollout plan: incremental steps, canary % targets, feature flags
- Backout plan: explicit commands/steps to revert, estimated restoration time
- Verification criteria: SLO metrics & smoke tests to validate success
- Stakeholders: list of teams & on-call contacts

Change review checklist
1. Verify dependencies and maintenance windows.
2. Confirm automated tests and staging sign-off.
3. Check capacity and performance impact estimates.
4. Confirm monitoring and alerting hooks are in place.

Emergency change postmortem
- Owner: 
- Reason for emergency: 
- Timeline: detection, decision, mitigation, closure
- Root cause and corrective actions
- Preventative measures and follow-up tickets

Data management and classification

Classification labels (company standard): PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, RESTRICTED

Handling rules by classification
- PUBLIC: No special controls. OK to publish on public docs.
- INTERNAL: Default classification for operational docs and internal dashboards. MFA required for access to internal systems.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Business-sensitive (customer lists, contracts). Encryption at rest and in transit required. RBAC enforced.
- RESTRICTED: Regulated PII/PHI or cryptographic key material. Additional controls: HSM/KMS, isolated network, stricter auditing, and access approvals from Security + Legal.

Data retention and deletion
- Default retention for non-regulated operational logs: 90 days hot, 365 days cold.
- Customer data retention follows contractual terms; for absence of a contract default to 2 years unless legal instructs otherwise.
- Data deletion request procedure: submit Data Deletion Request (DDR) to Data Governance; include dataset, owner, justification, and verification steps.

Analyst: sample data classification table
| Dataset | Classification | Owner | Retention | Access Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Developer logs | INTERNAL | Platform Team | 90d hot / 365d cold | Redaction of tokens required |
| Customer PII | RESTRICTED | Product Security | Contract-specific | KMS + audited access only |
| Public blog posts | PUBLIC | Marketing | Indefinite | Publicly accessible |

Procurement and expenses (operational rules + templates)

Principles
- Consolidate vendors where possible to reduce overhead and simplify security reviews.
- Favor annual contracts with predictable renewals where unit cost savings exceed 8%.
- Use approved vendor list for low-risk purchases; new vendors require onboarding checklist.

Procurement flow (summary)
1. Triage & justification: Requestor fills Procurement Request Form (PRF).
2. Pricing & alternatives: Procurement solicits 2–3 quotes for purchases > $10K.
3. Security & Legal review: Required if vendor accesses sensitive data.
4. Approval routing: Manager -> Procurement -> Finance -> Legal (as needed).
5. PO creation and vendor onboarding: Procurement issues PO and creates vendor profile.

Expense policy highlights
- Meal limits: $75 per person domestic; $125 per person international business travel.
- Ground transportation: prefer rideshare/rail; receipts required > $25.
- Lodging: mid-range business hotels; receipts required; exceptions pre-approved by manager.
- Corporate card use: follow the Corporate Card Policy; cardholder retains receipts for 90 days.

Vendor management and onboarding checklist
- Required documents: W-9 (US vendors) or equivalent tax forms, Certificate of Insurance, Security Questionnaires (if accessing data).
- Security posture review: completion of Security Questionnaire + baseline penetration scan or Attestation (depending on risk level).
- Contract templates: use Vendor Master Agreement (VMA) boilerplate and record negotiated deviations.
- Operational handoffs: assign vendor liaison, escalation contacts, and SLA targets.

Vendor risk tiers (examples)
- Tier 1 — Critical: vendor-hosted customer data or production infra. Requires annual audit and quarterly operational review.
- Tier 2 — Important: internal tooling with limited data access. Semi-annual review.
- Tier 3 — Commodity: office supplies, non-sensitive SaaS. Annual review.

Travel policy summary and approval template

Pre-trip approval steps
1. Employee submits Travel Request with itinerary and estimated costs.
2. Manager approves and confirms budget center code.
3. People Ops and Finance receive copy for advance booking and insurance.

Expense submission checklist
- Submit within 30 days of trip end.
- Attach itemized receipts for all charges.
- Include business purpose and attendee names.
- Unapproved upgrades or entertainment must be justified.

Travel risk and safety
- For high-risk regions, require Country Risk Approval from People Ops and Security.
- Employees traveling to restricted regions must complete pre-travel security brief and register with People Ops.

Templates and reusable artifacts (included inline for copy/paste)

1) Access Request (CSV-friendly single-line template)
Requestor, EmployeeID, System, Role, StartDate, EndDate, Manager, SecurityReviewer, Justification

2) Procurement Request (PRF)
- Requestor: 
- Business justification: 
- Vendor name (if known): 
- Estimated annual spend: 
- Budget center code: 
- Contract start/end: 
- Security classification: (PUBLIC/INTERNAL/CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED)

3) Change Request example (YAML)
change_id: CHG-20260212-0421
owner: infra-team
change_type: Normal
risk: Low
steps:
  - step: "Deploy canary to 5% of traffic"
  - step: "Observe latency and error rate for 30 minutes"
backout:
  - step: "Rollback to previous stable image"
verification:
  - metric: "p50_latency < 120ms"
  - metric: "error_rate < 0.5%"

4) Vendor Onboarding checklist (bullet version)
- Confirm legal entity and tax form
- Verify insurance levels
- Complete security questionnaire
- Create vendor record in ERP and add to approved vendor list
- Define escalation path and assign vendor liaison

Operational enactment and ownership

- Policy steward: Finance + Security co-own these templates and the approval matrix.
- Execution owners: Procurement (vendor + purchasing), IT/Platform (access provisioning), Security (data & vendor risk), People Ops (travel & safety).
- Review cadence: Annual policy review in Q1; ad-hoc after incidents.

How to contribute changes to this cookbook

1. Open an RFC in the Policies repository (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/rfc-policy-changes).
2. Draft proposed change and include impact analysis and owner.
3. Route to the policy steward for triage.
4. If accepted, schedule stakeholder review and update the canonical templates in the Template Library (link provided in related pages).
